findings.failure_path: For providers such as OpenAI, the reported total input-token count already includes cached tokens, while cached tokens are a nested subset. Treating that total as “uncached input” and applying the stated equation double-counts cache reads; providers that omit cache-write/read fields can instead be misclassified as uncached or “not cached at all.” This corrupts cache-read share, cost attribution, and regression decisions.
findings.smallest_fix: Define provider-adapter-normalized, disjoint counters before giving an equation: input_total, cache_read, cache_creation, and derived uncached. For overlapping counters derive uncached as total minus reported subsets; when fields are absent, record unknown rather than zero or “not cached,” and calculate cache-read share from the normalized total.

challenge_focus: Adversarial pass on the lane-3 candidate: (1) the batch checklist's create-idempotency and reconciliation items — a provider path where lookup-before-retry cannot run, or where usage reconciled by item and batch id still misstates cost; (2) the prompt-cache usage arithmetic and cache-read share — a provider whose counters overlap or omit fields, making the stated equation double-count or under-count; (3) the reconciled tool-set boundary — any surviving text licensing in-flight mutation or suffix-only reuse; (4) plan-then-execute binding and the trifecta negative test — an injected change that still reaches an external action; (5) the delegation fan-out gate, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission or over-broad cost; (6) register anchors, receipts, and rows — stale locators, unsupported claims, contradictions; (7) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
